extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors of commutative algebra (readers of Atiyah & MacDonald)
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed annotated commentary and errata on Atiyah & MacDonald’s Introduction to Commutative Algebra: collects corrected statements, proofs, example counterexamples, exercises and solutions, and references. Intended as supplementary notes for readers working through the textbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.9 (Jacobian radical characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: x ∈ R ⇐⇒ 1 − xy is a unit in A for all y ∈ A. (R denotes the Jacobson radical of A.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition is singled out as used multiple times. No further scoring guidance; used as a tool in later arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empty-family conventions for ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: The intersection and the product of the empty family of ideals is the unit ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark clarifies convention used in subsequent statements; important for edge cases in proofs involving empty intersections/products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-distributivity of sum and intersection in general rings
rubrics_metrics.description: In Z the operations ∩ and + distribute over each other, but this is not true in general rings. Example given in K[x,y] showing explicit strict inclusions: (x+y)∩(x)+(x+y)∩(y) ⊂ (x+y)∩((x)+(y)) (with explicit monomial/ideal calculations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a concrete counterexample to a naive algebraic identity; warns readers not to assume distributivity outside principal ideal domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem (Prop. 1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a commutative ring and a1,…,an ideals with ai+aj=A for i≠j. Then the natural morphism A → Π A/ai is surjective, and the intersection of the ai coincides with their product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: produce idempotent-like elements ai ≡ δij mod aj via the equality A = a1 + a2⋯an; second claim follows by multiplying equality by the intersection. Inductive argument for n>2 is indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime avoidance lemma (Prop. 1.11i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a commutative ring and S a multiplicatively closed additive subgroup. Given ideals a1,…,an with ai prime for i≥3: if S is not contained in any ai then S is not contained in their union. Weaker useful form: if an ideal a is not contained in any of prime ideals p1,…,pn then a is not contained in their union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction constructing si ∈ S avoiding unions of other ideals; explicit constructive proof given (s := s1⋯sn−1 + sn). Variant (weaker) is often sufficient in textbook uses; explicit construction for the ideal-version also given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primes contain factors of product (Prop. 1.11ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is prime and p ⊃ ∏_{i=1}^n a_i then p ⊃ a_i for some i. If p = ⋂ a_i then p = a_i for some i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard proposition recorded for later reference; used to deduce minimal-prime and primary decomposition facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient ideal identities and basic inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples and identities such as (1:b) = (1) = (a:0), (a:1)=a, and monotonicity (a⊂a', b⊂b' ⇒ (a:b) ⊂ (a':b')).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collected equalities and inclusions used repeatedly; readers are warned about strictness in examples to avoid false equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1.12 — identities for colon ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements: (i) a ⊂ (a:b); (ii) (a:b)b ⊂ a; (iii) ((a:b):c) = (a:bc) = ((a:c):b); (iv) (⋂_i a_i : b) = ⋂_i (a_i : b); (v) (a : ⋂_i b_i) = ⋂_i (a : b_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions left to reader; comments give explicit examples showing inclusions in (i) and (ii) can be strict (e.g. a=b=(0) or a=(1), b=(0) in a nonzero ring). Important anti-pattern: do not assume equalities in general without checking hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1.13 — properties of the radical r(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements: (i) r(a) ⊃ a; (ii) r(r(a)) = r(a); (iii) r(ab) = r(a∩b) = r(a) ∩ r(b); (iv) r(a) = (1) ⇔ a = (1); (v) r(a+b) = r(r(a)+r(b)); (vi) if p is prime, r(p^n) = p for all n>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard properties of radical and nilradical; solutions left to reader. Useful to decide containment and equality of ideals via radicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended ideal along ring morphism (definition of ae)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:A→B is a ring morphism and a is an ideal of A then the extended ideal ae in B is the ideal generated by f(α) for α∈a (ae := ( f(α) : α∈a ) ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition used throughout Chapter 1 comments; several properties and counterexamples about behavior of extension with respect to sums/intersections/products/colon/radical are discussed later (see Exercise 1.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1.18 — behaviour of ideal operations under extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple identities/containments for extension along f: (a1 + a2)e = ae_1 + ae_2, (a1∩a2)e ⊂ ae_1 ∩ ae_2, (a1a2)e = ae_1 ae_2, (a1:a2)e ⊂ (ae_1:ae_2), r(a)e ⊂ r(ae). Analogous list for contraction and comments on strictness. Sets E and C (sets of extended/contracted ideals) closed under certain operations as proved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: proofs use earlier propositions; the notes include multiple explicit counterexamples (rings K[X,Y]/various ideals, inclusions that are strict) showing the inclusions can be strict in practice. Important practical guidance: do not assume equalities unless hypotheses guarantee them; verify with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1.1 — units from nilpotents
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is nilpotent in A then 1+x is a unit in A. Consequently, the sum of a nilpotent element and a unit is a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short constructive proof: inverse of 1−x is ∑_{n≥0} x^n when x nilpotent. Use as a routine trick in polynomial/unit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1.2 — characterization of units, nilpotents, zero-divisors, primitive polynomials in A[x]
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) f ∈ A[x] is a unit ⇔ a0 is a unit in A and a1,…,an are nilpotent. (ii) f is nilpotent ⇔ all coefficients are nilpotent. (iii) f is a zero-divisor ⇔ there exists a≠0 in A with af=0. (iv) f primitive (coeffs generate (1)) and product: fg primitive ⇔ f and g primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: use degree arguments, consider reduction mod primes, and induction on coefficients; argument reduces to checking images in A/p[x]. These are standard and used later (Exercise 1.3 and other polynomial results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1.3 — generalization to multivariable polynomial rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalizes Exercise 1.2 to A[x1,…,xr]: unit condition becomes 'constant term unit and coefficients of all nonconstant monomials are nilpotent'; similar statements for nilpotent and zero-divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: reduce to one-variable case by specializing primes and using images in A/p[x1,…,xr]; use prime-reduction arguments. Useful pattern: reduce multivariable statements to the single-variable/principal coefficient case via prime ideal tests.
